style: Read clearly and naturally, at a moderate pace
lines: Welcome to Field Lines. Each object has a mass and a charge. The left board shows its gravity, and the right board shows its electric field.
Drag the objects to move them. Drag the small ring, the probe, to read the field at any spot.
Mass comes in only one sign, so gravity always pulls. Charge comes in two, so it can push or pull.
Twice as far away, the field is one quarter as strong, on both boards.
The probe starts at rest. Watch where each field sends it.
Here the pulls cancel, and the field is zero.
Here is why both laws use one over r squared. The same lines spread out over more area as you move away.
At twice the distance, the lines cover four times the area, so each patch gets one quarter of them.
Now with real numbers. Pick a pair and compare the gravity and electric forces between them.
Both forces changed by the same factor, so the ratio between them did not change.
In a hydrogen atom, the electric pull is about two times ten to the thirty nine times stronger than gravity.
Earth and the Moon are neutral overall, so their charges cancel and gravity is the force that is left.
Same objects, two laws. Drag the probe and compare the two readouts.
On the left, every mass pulls. Gravity looks exactly like a world where every charge is negative: all lines point in.
The electric board shows a dipole: lines run from plus to minus. The gravity board shows two masses that both pull.
Between two equal pulls there is a spot where they cancel. The field reads zero here.
Twice as far, one quarter the field. Both boards obey one over r squared.
Half as far, four times the field.
Starting from rest, the probe follows the field. Gravity only ever pulls it in.
On the center line the sideways pulls balance, so the probe falls through the middle and swings back and forth. Nudge it sideways and try again.
The probe sits still: the pulls cancel here.
That would put the probe off the board. Move it closer first.
The probe cannot go inside a disc, so it stopped at the disc edge.
Six objects is the limit. Remove one to add more.
The boards are empty. Use the Add buttons to place an object.
Move the Distance slider. The same 36 lines spread over more tiles as the screen moves away.
The dashed curve is 36 over r. The real curve falls faster, because the area grows as r squared, not as r.
The shape is the same for both laws. Only the constant in front changes.
Pick a pair. Both bars share one log scale, and each tick is ten more powers of ten.
Both forces follow one over r squared, so they change by the same factor.
The apple sits on the surface. Any closer and it would be inside Earth, where this formula does not apply.
